papers.title: Recovering Resting-State EEG During AM-tACS Using Dynamic Adaptive Stimulation Artifact Source Separation.
papers.summary: Developed DASASS, a dynamic adaptive stimulation artifact source separation framework combining recursive covariance updating, adaptive component selection, and wavelet multiband processing to recover resting-state EEG during amplitude-modulated tACS. DASASS achieved the lowest NRMSE and residual demodulated modulation among compared methods and preserved four canonical microstate topographies (spatial correlations 0.8643-0.9412) with artifact-free reference EEG.

papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: Proposed an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework using Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform features (approximate entropy, rhythm energy ratio, C0-complexity, zero-crossing rate) with representative single-channel selection. Single-channel detection accuracies reached 84.52% (F4) for schizophrenia, 86.54% (F4) for Parkinson's disease, and 93.10% (Fp1) for depression.

papers.title: Forecasting Next-Day Alcohol Craving in Individuals With Problematic Alcohol Use With Multimodal Data and a Tiny Recurrent Neural Network: Prospective Longitudinal Study.
papers.summary: Developed a tiny multimodal recurrent neural network forecasting next-day alcohol craving from 28-day smartphone digital phenotypes plus baseline EEG, HRV, and psychological measures in 60 participants with problematic alcohol use. The multimodal model outperformed the digital-phenotype-only model (accuracy 0.56 vs 0.45; MAE 0.68 vs 0.90), with improved accuracy in 72% of participants.

papers.title: Next generation Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with biophysically realistic somatic, dendritic and synaptic dynamics
papers.summary: Presents a substantially updated Human Neocortical Neurosolver canonical circuit model with electrophysiological and synaptic properties tuned to human tissue, adding L5 ET dendritic Ca2+ spikes and shorter L2/3 dendritic spikes. Demonstrates workflows for disentangling somatic, synaptic, and dendritic contributions to human EEG/MEG event-related responses and oscillations.

papers.title: Cross-cohort validation of EEG biomarkers using a pre-registered three-criterion framework: a demonstration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
papers.summary: Applied a pre-registered three-criterion framework (cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, cross-cohort effect consistency) to screen 18 EEG features for ALS biomarkers across three independent cohorts. Gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy met all criteria, while cross-cohort reliability differences (e.g., relative beta power ICC 0.09 vs 0.93) were large relative to disease-associated signal and bootstrap analyses showed selected-set sensitivity to sample composition.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.summary: Examined resting-state EEG spectral characteristics in 20 children with ASD and 15 typically developing children, and pre-post changes around a single 30-min Berard auditory integration training session using FOOOF spectral parameterization. ASD showed higher delta and lower theta/alpha/beta relative power at baseline; post-session delta decreased and beta/gamma increased, but aperiodic exponent and offset showed no significant changes.

papers.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes
papers.summary: Applied nonnegative tensor decomposition to clinical EEG from 455 patients, identifying four latent oscillatory factors that varied across FDG-PET-defined neurodegenerative phenotypes. A slowing index tracked a DLB-associated metabolic pattern, and the factors supported exploratory classification of dementia phenotypes with AUC > 0.8 for several contrasts.

papers.title: TARS-EEG: a tropical algebraic representation for EEG seizure detection.
papers.summary: Introduces TARS-EEG, an interpretable tropical algebraic representation that maps short EEG segments into multiscale max-plus and min-plus dilation, erosion, gradient, and residue profiles with a Tropical Seizure Index for seizure detection. Under recording-group-aware five-fold cross-validation, MLP reached 97.70% mean accuracy and XGBoost a ROC-AUC of 0.9926, outperforming individual neighbourhood-scale representations.

papers.title: Source-resolved electroencephalogram microstates reveal opposing prefrontal-posterior dynamics and a candidate temporal-to-precuneus pathway in disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: In high-density EEG from 33 disorders-of-consciousness patients and 19 controls, source-localized microstate analysis revealed opposing dynamics: right prefrontal microstate 3 was enhanced in vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome while parieto-occipital-temporal microstate 4 was higher in minimally conscious state, with microstate 4 occurrence discriminating the groups (AUC = 0.812). Hypothesis-generating Granger causality nominally implicated stronger right middle temporal-to-precuneus flow in minimally conscious state, though this did not survive network-level correction.

papers.title: Aperiodic Exponent as an EEG Marker of Interoceptive Attention during Gastric Fullness
papers.summary: Showed that the EEG aperiodic exponent flattens after water intake to fullness consistently across individuals, accompanied by increased vagal drive to peripheral organs measured via simultaneous gastric and cardiac recordings. Changes in cortical aperiodic exponent patterns were associated with changes in gastric oscillation frequency, suggesting the exponent as a noninvasive biomarker of gastric interoceptive attention.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Neonatal Seizure Detection: A Pragmatic Evaluation of Clinical Performance Tradeoffs in Clinical EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Evaluated three AI-based neonatal seizure detectors on 15,343 hours of continuous EEG from 169 neonates with encephalopathy, finding all identified ≥95% of seizure-positive infants but with differing tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and false alarm burden. NSD2 had the lowest false detections (3.2/day) but detected only 35% of seizures, whereas NSD1 and Persyst-15 detected 60-63% with higher false detections for NSD1 (46/day).

papers.title: A Neuroscientific Prior-Guided Multi-View Network With Structured Channel Selection for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposed SGA-MVTN, a neuroscientific prior-guided two-stage framework integrating a multi-view tower network with a structured genetic algorithm for topology-aware EEG channel selection in emotion recognition. Under leave-one-subject-out, full-channel MVTN achieved 87.91% on SEED and 71.09% on SEED-IV, and SGA-MVTN reduced channels by 54.84% while retaining 95.56% of full-channel accuracy.

papers.title: Wearable electrophysiology monitoring enabled by stretchable porous composite conductors.
papers.summary: Reported a porous AgNWs/PEDOT:PSS composite electrode with uniform conductive networks and cold-welded junctions, fabricated by template-assisted assembly, that dissipates stress and maintains stable performance at 50% strain over 5000 stretching cycles. The electrode enabled reliable ECG, EOG, and EMG monitoring for wearable electrophysiology.

papers.title: In-ear electroencephalography: a systematic review of technology, applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed 24 studies on in-ear (ear-EEG) technologies, documenting progress in device miniaturization and wearable design with applications in sleep monitoring, seizure detection, cognitive workload, fatigue monitoring, and emotion recognition. Remaining challenges include signal quality, spatial coverage, and motion artifacts, requiring further validation for broader clinical and real-world use.

papers.title: Orthographic repetition elicits enhancement without suppression at both the word- and character-levels in Chinese.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: Two EEG priming experiments with time-frequency analysis showed that orthographic repetition of Chinese words and characters elicits both N200 enhancement and enhanced theta-band power relative to control, whereas semantic and phonological priming did not, and partial orthographic repetition replicated both effects at the character level. These findings indicate orthographic repetition produces theta-band enhancement rather than suppression across word and character levels.

papers.title: Characteristics of EEG Microstate Analysis of Power Grip and Precision Grip Hand Movements from Motor Planning to Execution.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Used high-density EEG microstate analysis to compare precision grip and power grip across motor planning and execution in 24 healthy participants. Planning microstate sequences were identical for both grips but the fourth ERP microstate was longer in precision grip, while execution showed stronger MSC suppression, greater MSD activation, and distinct transition probabilities in precision grip, with Random Forest reaching 72.07% for precision grip versus rest.

papers.title: HRA-Former: Hierarchical Region-Aware Transformer with Structure-Preserving Multi-Stage Learning for EEG-Based Driver Fatigue Detection.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Developed HRA-Former, a hierarchical region-aware Transformer with structure-preserving multi-stage learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection, using electrode-to-region aggregation and a two-stage masked reconstruction and classification strategy. It achieved subject-dependent accuracies of 95.18% on SEED-VIG and 86.67% on an independently collected dataset, outperforming representative methods.

papers.title: Beyond Onset Timing: Longer Sound Envelope Duration Enhances Neural Representation of the Musical Beat.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: EEG in participants listening to rhythmic sequences showed that longer sound envelope duration enhanced neural beat periodicity even though this periodicity was not prominent in the acoustic envelope or a biomimetic auditory nerve model, indicating higher-level processing beyond onset timing. The results support a holistic account in which features beyond onset timing contribute to the internal representation of musical beat.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Model based Federated Learning Framework for Seizure-Type Classification.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposed a dual-branch model with federated learning for automatic seizure-type classification from multi-center EEG, integrating 1DCNN complexity features and 2DCNN brain-network topological features via dynamic attention fusion and using FedProx to handle non-IID data. The framework maintained 98.42% accuracy and 94.79% macro-F1 even under extremely unbalanced data.

papers.title: Retrieval practice is associated with attenuated stress-related inference impairment and stronger reactivation of bridge-related category information
papers.summary: Acute stress impaired A-C inference accuracy and speed and disrupted rapid EEG reactivation of bridge element B, while retrieval practice buffered these stress effects and enhanced bridge reactivation beyond the non-stress condition.

papers.title: Healthy aging, processing speed, and mnemonic brain state engagement.
papers.summary: EEG with multivariate decoding in younger and older adults explicitly encoding and retrieving objects under variable stimulus durations showed that, under time constraints, older adults under-recruited a young adult-like retrieval state when task-relevant but over-recruited an idiosyncratic retrieval state when task-irrelevant. Findings indicate older adults retain encoding and retrieval brain states but need more processing time to initiate and maintain goal-relevant mnemonic states.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.summary: In an open-label, single-arm trial, 19 patients with treatment-resistant depression received 6-12 sessions of 100-Hz magnetic seizure therapy, with significant symptom reductions (HAMD-24 40.53 to 22.53; MADRS 35.68 to 20.68) and response rates of 42.1-57.9%. Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity at Fz/FCz was lower post-treatment only at an uncorrected threshold and did not survive FDR correction.

papers.title: Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Biophysical Mechanisms, Neural Effects, and Clinical Translation.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This review synthesizes progress on low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation, covering biophysical mechanisms, neurophysiological effects across cellular, circuit, and systems levels, and network-level consequences revealed by optical imaging, electrophysiology, EEG source imaging, and fMRI. It argues that imaging-based biomarkers of target engagement and circuit modulation are advancing TUS toward a translational inflection point as both a causal neuroscience tool and clinical neuromodulation therapy.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.summary: EEG compared long-term Tibetan Buddhist monks practicing Tantra (n=21) versus Sutra (n=20) meditation in a between-groups and within-subjects design, finding the Tantra group had consistently lower alpha power across meditation and baseline conditions. Within subjects, only the Tantra group showed increased individual alpha peak frequency in occipital leads during meditation, decreasing afterward; between-group differences are interpreted as enduring meditative traits.

papers.title: Thalamic Reticular Nucleus Excitability and Cholinergic Signaling are Disrupted in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease Neuropathology.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Using slice electrophysiology in APP transgenic mice, the study found that thalamic reticular nucleus core neurons show reduced intrinsic excitability and that cholinergic afferents evoke a larger muscarinic receptor-mediated inhibitory component, delaying TRN firing in a mouse model of early Alzheimer's disease neuropathology.

papers.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
papers.summary: Recorded eye-tracking and EEG while participants maintained up to three object orientations in working memory, finding that miniature gaze patterns encoded all three items throughout the delay with load and serial-position effects, whereas EEG encoding was short-lived. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, eye movements did not alternate between items and gaze encoding strength was not modulated by frontal theta.

papers.title: Disrupted activation of dot perspective task-related EEG generators in forensic patients with borderline personality disorder.
papers.summary: Coupled the dot-perspective task with high-density EEG and inverse source localization to examine neural generators of altercentric and egocentric biases in 24 healthy controls and 14 forensic male BPD patients. In BPD patients no significant differential generator activation was observed for the biases, unlike controls, suggesting reduced mobilization of brain resources when treating Self-Other discrepancy.

papers.title: Neural integration of musical and lyrical emotion: semantic-acoustic congruence in song processing.
papers.summary: This mini review synthesizes behavioral, EEG/ERP, MEG, and functional neuroimaging evidence on how musical-acoustic structure, lyrical semantics, and vocal prosody interact during song emotion processing, and proposes a provisional dynamic weighted-integration account. It reports limited direct neural evidence specifically manipulating music-lyric emotional congruence.

papers.title: Epileptiform Discharges in Seizure-Free Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and the Role of Antiseizure Medications.
papers.journal: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 50 seizure-free children with autism spectrum disorder, epileptiform discharges were detected in 48% by EEG; among the 9 children adherent to antiseizure medications after 6 months, all showed EEG improvement and significant reductions in CARS-2 severity scores.

papers.title: Disaggregating between- and within- person effects of ovarian hormones on the association between worry and error-related brain activity in a female sample.
papers.summary: Examined how between- and within-person differences in estradiol and progesterone across the menstrual cycle moderate the association between worry and the error-related negativity in 132 women using daily saliva sampling, the Penn State Worry Questionnaire, and Flanker-task EEG. Worry interacted with estradiol (p=.006) and progesterone (p<.001) such that worry was associated with an enlarged ERN at lower estradiol and higher average progesterone, with no significant within-person effects.

papers.title: A high-throughput all-optical platform for mapping gene perturbations to electrophysiology
papers.summary: Developed a high-throughput all-optical electrophysiology platform combining an engineered hiPSC line (inducible NGN2, CRISPRi, Voltron2/CheRiff) with wide-field voltage imaging and automated analysis, recording ~1,500 spiking neurons at 800 Hz. Arrayed knockdown of five sodium- and potassium-channel genes produced distinct electrophysiological phenotypes, establishing a scalable platform for functional genomics.

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: A retrospective cohort using the Pediatric Health Information System found that only 12.5% of 13,202 neonates with complex congenital heart disease underwent EEG monitoring, with utilization varying from 0% to over 40% across hospitals and rising from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025 while seizure detection among monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26%.

papers.title: Psychosis of Epilepsy: A Review of Diagnosis and Management.
papers.summary: Review of the diagnosis and management of psychosis of epilepsy (POE), covering preictal, ictal, postictal, and interictal subtypes and their EEG and clinical features. Recommends risperidone as the antipsychotic with the lowest seizure prevalence and discusses optimal dosing of AEDs (oxcarbazepine, carbamazepine, valproic acid, lamotrigine) in POE.

papers.title: Aphasic status epilepticus presenting with prominent psychiatric symptoms: A case report.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: Case report of a 49-year-old woman with aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) presenting predominantly with agitation, irritability, and disorganized thinking after a head injury. EEG showed left-dominant periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges; antiseizure treatment resolved symptoms, with no recurrence for >2 years after medication optimization.

papers.title: Rapidly progressive sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease overshadowed by a grief reaction and parkinsonism: a case report.
papers.journal: Neuropsychiatrie : Klinik, Diagnostik, Therapie und Rehabilitation : Organ der Gesellschaft Osterreichischer Nervenarzte und Psychiater
papers.summary: This case report describes a 60-year-old man with rapidly progressive sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease initially obscured by a grief reaction and a long-standing presumed Parkinson's disease diagnosis, confirmed by periodic triphasic EEG activity, diffusion restriction on MRI, and a positive CSF RT-QuIC assay.

papers.title: Current strategies of cerebral oxygenation monitoring in general intensive care units: a narrative review.
papers.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized physiological principles, monitoring modalities, and clinical applications of cerebral oxygenation monitoring across neurocritical care and perioperative settings, drawing on 58 studies published 2010-2025. It concluded that brain tissue oxygen tension (<25 mmHg indicating high risk), jugular bulb oximetry, and near-infrared spectroscopy offer complementary information, and recommended multimodal neuromonitoring plus standardized thresholds and protocolized prospective outcome research.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Conducted an international 39-item survey of 66 epilepsy surgery centers (38 North American, 28 European) to compare stereo-EEG practices, finding North American centers more often used robotic implantation and had higher volumes, while European centers had more SEEG experience, more dedicated readers, and more frequent SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation. Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequent in North America unadjusted but not after adjustment for experience and volume.

papers.title: Does Neurobiological Evidence Support the Diagnostic Distinction Between Hoarding Disorder and OCD? A Critical Narrative Review of Genetic, Neuroimaging, and Neuropsychological Findings.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review assessed genetic, neuroimaging, and neuropsychological evidence for the DSM-5 separation of hoarding disorder from OCD. It found only supplementary, not definitive, neurobiological support—estimates such as ~26%-48% twin heritability and 11% SNP-based heritability are compatible with a heritable polygenic trait, imaging differences are small and unconverged, and the most recent systematic review reported no significant impairment on most cognitive tests in HD.

papers.title: Macroscopic pulmonary fat embolism following cemented hemiarthroplasty for pathological femoral fracture: A case report with dual-energy CT spectral analysis.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 73-year-old woman with metastatic NSCLC who developed severe hemodynamic instability during cement pressurization for hemiarthroplasty of a pathological proximal femoral lesion, consistent with bone cement implantation syndrome, and recovered with supportive care. Dual-energy CT pulmonary angiography showed a 30 × 15 mm right main pulmonary artery filling defect with mean attenuation of -86.6 HU, progressively more negative CT numbers at lower photon energies, and persistence on virtual noncontrast images, supporting a fatty embolus.

papers.title: Aluminum Foil Substrates Support Solvent-Free Raman Analysis of Skin Lipids.
papers.summary: This technical note demonstrated that aluminum foil substrates enable direct, solvent-free sampling and Raman spectroscopic analysis of human sebum, preserving lipid, protein, and carotenoid vibrational signatures. In three volunteers, solvent-free sampling yielded more intense and chemically rich spectra than chloroform/methanol or diethyl ether extraction, which attenuated signals and introduced solvent-dependent compositional bias in carbonyl and hydrocarbon stretching regions.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
